questions.q: What does Continuous Integration (CI) mean for a database project, specifically?
options: Automatically building the .sqlproj on every proposed change to validate the schema is internally consistent
Automatically deploying every commit straight to production
Manually reviewing every schema change by hand before it's committed
Continuously running backups of the production database
questions.explain: CI validates, it doesn't deploy — for databases that validation is building the project and catching broken references.

questions.q: What is the difference between Continuous Deployment and Continuous Delivery, per this lesson?
options: Continuous Deployment applies a validated change automatically with no human trigger; Continuous Delivery is automated up to production, then requires a deliberate approval
They are the same thing with two different names
Continuous Delivery only applies to application code, never to databases
Continuous Deployment requires a human to manually write the deployment script every time
questions.explain: The distinction is whether the final production step happens fully automatically or waits for a deliberate human trigger.

questions.q: Why do many teams choose Continuous Delivery over full Continuous Deployment for a database's production step?
options: A bad database change is much harder to fully undo than a bad stateless application deployment
SQL Server technically prevents any form of automated deployment
Continuous Delivery is required by all database licensing agreements
There is no real reason; it's purely a matter of preference with no practical basis
questions.explain: Given how difficult some schema changes are to reverse, teams often keep a deliberate human approval gate before production specifically.

questions.q: In the realistic pipeline this lesson describes, what happens immediately after CI validates a change?
options: The change deploys automatically to a test/staging environment, where automated tests run
The change is immediately and irreversibly applied to production
The pull request is automatically deleted
A DBA must manually re-type the entire migration script
questions.explain: After CI passes, the pipeline deploys to test/staging first, runs tests, and only then proceeds toward production.

questions.q: How does CI/CD relate to the code review gate covered in Lesson 16?
options: CI/CD automates what happens after a change is reviewed and merged — it doesn't replace the human review step
CI/CD entirely replaces the need for code review
CI/CD happens before code review, not after
CI/CD and code review are unrelated processes that never interact
questions.explain: The review gate remains the human checkpoint; CI/CD removes the manual, error-prone steps that follow approval.
